'''''The Moon & Antarctica''''' is the third [[studio album]] by American [[rock music|rock]] band [[Modest Mouse]], released on June 13, 2000, by [[Epic Records]].

''The Moon & Antarctica'' peaked at number 120 on the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]],<ref name="chart"/> and received acclaim from critics,<ref name="MC"/> who praised its subject matter and change in sound from earlier albums and frontman [[Isaac Brock (musician)|Isaac Brock]]'s introspective lyrics. It was also hailed for being an expansion of the band's sound, much due to their new major label budget as well as the production of [[Brian Deck]]. In 2021, ''[[NME]]'' referred to it as "one of the greatest records ever made".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/modest-mouse-the-golden-casket-review-2972977|title=Modest Mouse – 'The Golden Casket' review: the spiritual sequel to their breakout hit|website=Nme.com|date=22 June 2021|access-date=12 November 2021}}</ref>

==Background and recording==
The album was the band's first released by a major record label, being issued on [[Epic Records]].<ref name="Cohen, Jonathan 2000">Cohen, Jonathan. "Epic To Mine Indie Base For Modest Mouse Set." Billboard 112.25 (2000): 24. Academic Search Premier. Web. 2 Nov. 2011</ref>

The album was produced by [[Brian Deck]], who first met the band at a concert in [[Detroit]]. "We ended up on a bill together at [[The Magic Stick]] in Detroit, and we got along really well, we hung out till the end of the night—and maybe consumed a fair amount of beer together" says Deck.<ref name="wood">Wood, Mikael. "[https://www.myspace.com/music/blog/2010/8/17/rewind-modest-mouse-and-the-moon-antarctica Rewind: Modest Mouse and The Moon and Antarctica.]" par. 5. myspace.com. 17 Aug 2010. Web. 14 Nov 2011.</ref> Deck and Brock fell out of touch shortly thereafter, but reconnected a few years later, when Brock invited [[Califone]] (which included several members of Deck's band Red Red Meat) to hit the road as Modest Mouse's opening act.

The album was the first project to be recorded in [[Clava Studios]] in [[Chicago]].<ref name="weldon">Weldon, Rick. "The Making Of The Moon." Electronic Musician 17.1 (2001): 114. Academic Search Premier. Web. 2 Nov. 2011.</ref> When Modest Mouse band members arrived for the recording, the studio was not completely finished.<ref name="weldon" /> Though Deck was mostly producing under [[Perishable Records]] at the time, and the studio was built mostly for Perishable projects, Deck had no problems producing under [[Epic Records]]. Despite being under a major label the band "remains largely self-managed and still drive themselves across the country on tour",<ref name="Cohen, Jonathan 2000" /> and Brock was fairly involved in the mixing process. Deck said of Brock's involvement that, "By the end of making the record, he was able to mastermind some cool maneuvers with plug-ins and [[Pro Tools]]. It wasn't so much that he was mixing, but he could look at a song, understand the musical event that he wanted to make happen, understand the tools at his disposal, relate it in a way that I could understand, and make it happen pretty quickly."<ref name="Cohen, Jonathan 2000" />

In the middle of recording, Brock was attacked and had his jaw broken by a group of ruffians hanging out at a park across the street from where the band were staying in [[Chicago]].<ref>Brock, Isaac. Interview by Josh Model. A.V. Club. The Onion, 2004. Web. Oct 26, 2011.</ref> "It laid him up in the hospital for a week," Deck says. "Then his jaw was wired shut for two or three months."<ref name="weldon" />

The recording for the album took 5 months, beginning in July 1999 and running until November 1999.<ref>News. modestmousemusic.com. Sony Music Entertainment Inc. 2011. Online. November 2, 2011.</ref>

==Music and lyrics==
Despite the fans' common concern that the switch to a major record label would change the band's unique sound, Isaac Brock assured fans that this would not be the case, "I don't think the new album is at all overpolished or anything. We spent more time getting crazy sounds than making things sound polished."<ref name="Cohen, Jonathan 2000" /> [[AllMusic]] described the album's sound as "strangely subdued". The album's mood has been described as "melancholy", and its textures have been called "[[wikt:atmospheric|atmospheric]]" and "[[wikt:angular|angular]]". Lyrical themes explored on the album include [[death]] and the [[afterlife]].<ref>{{Citation |title=The Moon & Antarctica - Modest Mouse {{!}} Album {{!}} AllMusic |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-moon-antarctica-mw0000065059 |access-date=2025-01-01 |language=en}}</ref>

''The Moon & Antarctica'' was released to acclaim from music critics. [[Metacritic]], which assigns a normalised rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, reported an average score of 82 based on 22 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref name="MC"/> Stephen Thompson of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' felt that ''The Moon & Antarctica'' was the band's "weirdest record yet" and would downplay worries that Modest Mouse's move to a major label "would smooth out the edges of the group's brash, jerky sound", calling it a "sort of concept album about cold and distant places" held together by "a strange sort of precision, lending lurching power to the strongest material."<ref name="thompsen">{{cite journal |url=https://www.avclub.com/modest-mouse-the-moon-antarctica-1798192415 |title=Modest Mouse: The Moon & Antarctica |journal=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=June 13, 2000 |access-date=July 24, 2015 |last=Thompson |first=Stephen}}</ref> Nick Catucci of ''[[The Village Voice]]'' noted the album's more streamlined production, in contrast to the [[lo-fi (audio)|lo-fi]] quality of their previous work, and complimented the fact that "the studio scrubbing leaves no noticeable film; even the effects—like the spacey guitar that launches 'Gravity Rides Everything'—ring true."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.villagevoice.com/music/think-about-pavement-6394804 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304080856/http://www.villagevoice.com/music/think-about-pavement-6394804 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |title=Think About Pavement |work=[[The Village Voice]] |date=May 16, 2000 |access-date=November 2, 2015 |last=Ctucci |first=Nick}}</ref> Heather Phares of [[AllMusic]] felt that the production enhanced the album's introspective tone and called the album "their most cohesive collection of songs to date" and "an impressive, if flawed, map of Modest Mouse's ambitions and fears."<ref name="phares" /> ''[[Melody Maker]]'' praised ''The Moon & Antarctica'' as being "beyond anything else they've ever achieved".<ref name="MM"/>

[[Robert Christgau]] of ''The Village Voice'' remarked that Isaac Brock "may be every bit the ass he claims, but basically he seems chagrined that he was ever so inept or unlucky as to get caught up in this, as the saying goes, downward spiral. And unlike other rock pessimists we might name, he's so modest about it that he ends up with an uplifting representation of human life as damn shame."<ref name="robertchristgau"/> Brent DiCrescenzo of ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' described ''The Moon & Antarctica'' as an "intoxicating mix of uncertainty and confidence".<ref name="Pitchfork"/> ''[[LA Weekly]]''{{'}}s Rita Neyler called the album "darker and colder" than the band's previous work, but nonetheless representative of "the very particular blend of peculiar lyrics and uncompromising rock that consistently weaves through all their records."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.laweekly.com/ink/00/30/music-cheyney.shtml |title=Modest Mouse: The Moon and Antarctica (Epic) |work=[[LA Weekly]] |date=June 16–22, 2000 |access-date=November 2, 2015 |last=Neyter |first=Rita |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010211124837/http://www.laweekly.com/ink/00/30/music-cheyney.shtml |archive-date=February 11, 2001}}</ref> In a negative review, ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]''{{'}}s Chris Ryan felt that "mistaking subject for style, Modest Mouse has chosen to accentuate on a tendency to drift rather than an ability to write emotionally effective songs."<ref name="spin">{{cite journal |url=http://www.spin.com/heavy/bigrotation/2000/06/19/1/index.html |title=Heavy Rotation {{!}} Modest Mouse {{!}} The Moon and Antarctica {{!}} Epic |journal=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]] |date=June 19, 2000 |access-date=July 24, 2015 |last=Ryan |first=Chris |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001022003505/http://www.spin.com/heavy/bigrotation/2000/06/19/1/index.html |archive-date=October 22, 2000}}</ref>

===Accolades===
''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' ranked ''The Moon & Antarctica'' as the third best album of 2000, trailing ''[[Kid A]]'' by [[Radiohead]] and ''[[Ágætis byrjun]]'' by [[Sigur Rós]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/5816-top-20-albums-of-2000/ |title=Top 200 Albums of 2000 |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=January 1, 2001 |access-date=October 4, 2009}}</ref> The album ranked at number 49 on ''[[The Village Voice]]''{{'}}s [[Pazz & Jop]] year-end critics' poll.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://villagevoice.com/specials/pazznjop/00/albums2.php3 |title=Pazz & Jop 2000 |work=[[The Village Voice]] |access-date=May 30, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010223221633/http://villagevoice.com/specials/pazznjop/00/albums2.php3 |archive-date=February 23, 2001}}</ref> ''Pitchfork'' later named it the seventh best album of the years 2000 through 2004 and the sixth best album of the decade.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pitchfork.com/features/staff-lists/5956-the-top-100-albums-of-2000-04-part-one/10/ |title=The Top 100 Albums of 2000–04 |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=February 7, 2005 |access-date=October 4, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://pitchfork.com/features/staff-lists/7710-the-top-200-albums-of-the-2000s-20-1/2/ |title=The Top 200 Albums of the 2000s: 20–1 |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=October 2, 2009 |access-date=October 2, 2009 |archive-date=October 4, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091004234842/http://pitchfork.com/features/staff-lists/7710-the-top-200-albums-of-the-2000s-20-1/2 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''[[Tiny Mix Tapes]]'' placed it at number 51 on their decade-end list.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tinymixtapes.com/features/favorite-100-albums-2000-2009-60-41 |title=Favorite 100 Albums of 2000–2009: 60–41 |work=[[Tiny Mix Tapes]] |date=February 10, 2010 |access-date=November 11, 2011}}</ref> ''The Moon & Antarctica'' was included in ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'''s "The New Classics", a list of the one hundred best albums released within 1983 to 2008.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.ew.com/article/2007/06/18/new-classics-music |title=The New Classics: Music — The 100 best albums from 1983 to 2008 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=June 17, 2008 |access-date=October 4, 2009}}</ref> [[Rhapsody (online music service)|Rhapsody]] ranked the album at number four on its "Alt/Indie's Best Albums of the Decade" list.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.rhapsody.com/2009/11/altindie.html |title=Alt/Indie's Best Albums of the Decade |publisher=[[Rhapsody (online music service)|Rhapsody]] |access-date=January 12, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091129004450/http://blog.rhapsody.com/2009/11/altindie.html |archive-date=November 29, 2009}}</ref>

As of October 2006 the album has sold 492,000 copies in United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6g0EAAAAMBAJ&q=modest+mouse+The+Lonesome+Crowded+West+album+sales&pg=PA26|title=Rock Climbing|publisher=Billboard |page=26|first=Jonathan|last=Cohen|date=14 October 2006|access-date=9 September 2019}}</ref> In March 2009, ''The Moon & Antarctica'' was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&se=Modest+Mouse#search_section |title=Gold & Platinum: Modest Mouse |publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America]] |access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref> In 2015, [[Vitamin String Quartet]] paid tribute to the album by covering it in its entirety.

==Reissues==
Isaac Brock was dissatisfied with the final mix and the album artwork for ''The Moon & Antarctica'' following its original 2000 release.<ref name="filter">
{{cite journal |url=http://www.filter-mag.com/index.php?id=6755&c=2 |title=True Glue: John Wayne and a Not So Modest Mouse |journal=[[Filter (magazine)|Filter]] |access-date=October 4, 2009 |last=Leckart |first=Steve |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027183015/http://www.filter-mag.com/index.php?id=6755&c=2 |archive-date=October 27, 2007 }}</ref> According to an interview given in ''[[Filter (magazine)|Filter]]'' in 2004, he intended to remix the album "on his own time, using his own money, simply to have a copy he alone could hear."<ref name="filter" /> Epic Records then offered to remaster the album to CD, reissuing it on March 9, 2004, with remastered audio, new artwork and four additional tracks from a [[BBC Radio 1]] session.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lasvegasmercury.com/2004/MERC-May-13-Thu-2004/23855023.html |title=CDVS: Jawbreaker vs. Modest Mouse |work=Las Vegas Mercury |date=May 13, 2004 |access-date=October 4, 2009 |last=Prevatt |first=Mike}}</ref> Stephen M. Deusner of ''Pitchfork'' rated the remastered edition a 5.0 out of 10, writing highly of the original album itself but questioning the decision to re-release it just four years after its initial release, calling the additional material "paltry offerings" and commenting that "no one was really asking for it, and there's simply not enough here to justify the expense or even a rating as high as the original."<ref name="Deusner">{{cite web |url=http://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/5362-the-moon-antarctica-expanded-edition/ |title=Modest Mouse: The Moon & Antarctica [Expanded Edition] |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=March 29, 2004 |access-date=July 24, 2015 |last=Deusner |first=Stephen M.}}</ref>

A vinyl and CD reissue was released on April 13, 2010, to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the album, with both versions reverting to the original artwork and track listing.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.epicrecords.com/news/cd-reissue-moon-antarctica-now-available-purchase |title=CD Reissue of The Moon & Antarctica Available Now |publisher=[[Epic Records]] |access-date=May 6, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728035217/http://www.epicrecords.com/news/cd-reissue-moon-antarctica-now-available-purchase |archive-date=July 28, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 27, 2015, Music on Vinyl reissued the album in two different variations in Europe, with one featuring remastered audio on transparent 180g vinyl in a production run limited to 500 pressings, and the other on standard black vinyl.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thelimitedpress.com/modest-mouse-the-moon-antarctica-music-on-vinyl-ltd-to-500/ |title= Modest Mouse - The Moon & Antarctica // Music On Vinyl [LTD To 500] |publisher=The Limited Press |access-date=March 16, 2015}}</ref> Both removed the "locked groove" previously found on side 1 at the end of "Perfect Disguise".
